target.title: fix(codex): honor timeoutSeconds when timeoutMs is absent in dynamic tool calls
target.body:
Fixes #98864

This PR keeps the fix shape narrow to match #98864 exactly: `timeoutSeconds` is only used as the seconds-form fallback for `timeoutMs`, without adding extra watchdog grace beyond the configured bound.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tool calls can pass `timeoutSeconds` without `timeoutMs`. The app-server hard timeout reader only checked `timeoutMs`, so seconds-form tool budgets were ignored and the call fell back to the default dynamic-tool watchdog instead of honoring the configured bound.

This affected both the main Codex app-server path and the side-question path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change updates the dynamic tool timeout readers so `timeoutSeconds` is treated as the seconds-form equivalent of `timeoutMs` when `timeoutMs` is absent.

The fix intentionally keeps the issue's narrow semantics:
- `timeoutMs` still has precedence when present
- `timeoutSeconds` falls back to the same hard-timeout reader only when `timeoutMs` is absent
- no extra grace is added beyond the configured timeout bound
- invalid or non-positive `timeoutSeconds` values are ignored and fall back to existing defaults

The side-question timeout path now reuses the same timeout readers so the two Codex dynamic-tool entry points do not drift.

## User Impact

Codex dynamic tool calls that provide only `timeoutSeconds` now honor that timeout instead of silently falling back to the default 90-second watchdog.

This keeps timeout behavior aligned with the issue contract and avoids extending the configured timeout beyond the value the caller supplied.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Focused regression coverage added for:
- `timeoutSeconds` fallback when `timeoutMs` is absent
- `timeoutMs` precedence over `timeoutSeconds`
- invalid `timeoutSeconds` values falling back to existing defaults
- side-question dynamic tool timeout parity with the main path

What was not tested:
- live end-to-end Codex app-server traffic with a real model
